notes: Generated by tools/tubuild.py create. See the file's own header comment for what was and was not reconciled, and notes/translation-unit-reconstruction-plan.md section 7.3 for what this generator does and does not attempt to resolve automatically.

Second key-function-TU pilot after ov017/daObjKsWater_c, same shape as daObjKm2_Ami_Bou_c/daObjKsWater_c: compiler_only_output covers D2Ev (byte-identical to D1, no ROM home, no inbound reloc). externalized_output covers the eight inherited vague-linkage RTTI records shared with the fBase_c/dBase_c/dActor_c/dBgActor_c hierarchy (arm9/ov002 canonical addresses, identical structure to daObjKsWater_c's own -- confirmed via a live ELF read of this TU's compiled object, not assumed). daObjYajirusi_c's own new _ZTI15daObjYajirusi_c/_ZTS15daObjYajirusi_c/_ZTV15daObjYajirusi_c stay unlicensed -- same as every prior key-function-TU pilot -- because no policy mechanism licenses a class's first-emitted vtable yet (Phase F, plan sec 15). NEW CASE NOT SEEN IN EITHER PRIOR PILOT: _ZN7Vector3D1Ev is also unlicensed. It is types.h's inline `~Vector3(){}`, re-emitted by every TU that destroys a Vector3, and it DOES have a configured ROM home (arm9 0x020072c0) -- confirmed identical body (`bx lr`) and zero inbound relocations within this TU via the same ELF read. Neither policy schema fits it: compiler_only_output refuses any symbol with a configured ROM home (it is not compiler-only), and externalized_output is restricted to _ZTI/_ZTS objects by its own validation, not .text functions. Left unlicensed alongside this TU's own vtable/RTTI; widening one of the two policy schemas (or adding a third) to cover a compiler-duplicated ordinary function is follow-up work, not attempted here. Render()/CleanupResources() were reconciled against the real header before verifying: the generator's local shadow struct pair (Base/Derived, standing in for the real inherited Model member) is gone in favour of `mModel.Render(0)`, matching daObjKsWater_c's precedent; and CleanupResources' mMeshCollider access, which the generator wrote as a raw offset cast to `dBgW*`, is now the plain member calls `mMeshCollider.IsEnabled()`/`.Disable()` -- the raw-cast form was ALSO a latent correctness bug once the file-table externs were retyped to `ArrowSignFileColumn`, not just a readability issue: the legacy file's byte-offset pointer arithmetic assumed a `char[]` base type, and multiplying an already-struct-typed pointer by 0xc again overshot every row lookup, which is what verify's first pass caught as a 999-word DIFF.

Superseded for production (this promotion): the Phase-F mechanism the pilot note above says did not exist now does -- compiler_only_output carries Vector3D1 as deadstrip-duplicate and all eleven data records as deadstrip-data (daBar_c shape: every record has a configured ROM home outside the claimed .text span, verified row by row against config/**/symbols.txt and this TU's own compiled ELF). The externalized_output block below stays as the partitioned-link pilot evidence; production text-only isolation reads compiler_only_output. Twin _L factory folded (see boundary_evidence); promoted_source moved off the coined stem by the S21 rename.

Coined parameter spellings disclosed: _ZN15daObjYajirusi_c11OnAttacked1ER8dActor_c and _ZN15daObjYajirusi_c15OnHitByMegaCharER6Player encode reference parameters. A reference and a pointer mangle differently but generate identical ARM for these bodies, so the bytes are silent on which the original source wrote. Class ownership, vtable slot identity (slots 22 and 27), bodies and relocations are proven; the exact original English names and the reference spellings are not. Same disclosure on the declarations (include/daObjYajirusi_c.h) and the why column of symbols/actor_renames.tsv.

Native initialization owns the four eight-byte model/collision handles and their four 12-byte registration nodes, in the original model/model/collision/collision construction order. Local resource-family type spellings are inferred ABI views; exact manifest aliases bind their ordinary C++ constructors/destructors to the original functions. The compiler emits the original .init and .ctor; the handwritten shard is retired. File-table column symbols and all actor methods remain unchanged.

INTACT RTTI POLICY. Eight inherited RTTI/type-name records previously appeared both as compiler_only_output deadstrip-data and as exact externalized_output canonical-imports. The text-only path ignored the latter; intact production correctly refused processing the same definitions twice. Retain the stricter existing externalized_output policies (exact type, binding, size, bytes and relocation destinations), removing only the eight duplicate generic policy rows. The inherited partial_isolation block records an older 11-shard experiment and is not current production proof; the new intact linkcheck is authoritative for this candidate.

include/types.h declares Vector3's destructor and leaves it empty, so every TU that destroys a Vector3 re-emits it as vague linkage (STB_LOPROC, 4 bytes). This TU destroys two Vector3 automatics: pos and dustPos in daObjYajirusi_c::Kill (ov098:0x02137ccc). The cartridge keeps exactly one copy, arm9:0x020072c0, kind:function(arm,size=0x4) -- the 4-byte `bx lr` body -- and an enrolled source already owns it, so rombuild compares this object's copy against those cartridge bytes and refuses anything but byte-identical vague-linkage output before discarding the duplicate. Home count taken from tools/relocs.py load_symbol_homes(), the index the gate itself reads: exactly 1, across all 106 checked-in symbols.txt files (arm9, itcm, dtcm and ov000-ov102), which is what selects deadstrip-duplicate over a plain deadstrip.
